nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment and hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (30 mm × 10 mm × 0.5 mm) was sonicated in a 1.0 M HCl aqueous solution for 40 min to remove the surface oxide layer and then washed with deionized water to remove residual HCl. By dissolving Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O, and RuCl3·xH2O in 30 ml deionized water, we obtained a solution with 40 mM of Ni, 10 mM of Mo, and 0.5 mM of Ru in a hydrothermal autoclave. After adding the cleaned Ni foam to the mixed solution, the system reacted for 6 h at 150°C in an oven.

nodes.name: Ar/H2 reduction annealing
nodes.procedure: The catalyst was put into a quartz tube furnace and purged with Ar (300 sccm) before annealing in an H2/Ar atmosphere (v/v, 5 sccm/95 sccm) at 500°C for 30 min. After the annealing process, the H2 was turned off and the furnace cooled to room temperature in an Ar flow.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH + seawater (LSV)

reference_electrode.value: Hg/HgO (1.0 M KOH) with salt bridge

nodes.source_text: Figure 2a shows the catalytic activity of RuMoNi, commercial RuO₂, and Ni foam in a 1.0 M KOH + seawater electrolyte (Supplementary Fig. 12, Supplementary Table 1). The RuMoNi electrocatalyst only requires an overpotential of 245 mV to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... At 1.70 V vs. RHE, RuMoNi delivers a high current density of 1000 mA cm⁻²... The Tafel slope of RuMoNi (41.2 mV dec⁻¹) is the smallest one among the three samples.

nodes.description: OER durability at 500 mA/cm² in 1.0 M KOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: The results show that it maintains a high activity with negligible performance decay after a stability test for 3000 h at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² in a 1.0 M KOH + seawater electrolyte... the Dv of RuMoNi is only 0.64 μV h⁻¹... the cell voltage would suffer an increase as small as 56 mV after operation for 10 years.

nodes.description: OER durability at different temperatures in 1.0 M KOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: Figure 3c shows that the activity of RuMoNi electrocatalyst at 500 mA cm⁻² remains steady at temperatures of 40, 60, and 80 °C.

nodes.description: OER durability in high salinity 1.0 M KOH + 2.0 M NaCl
nodes.source_text: we performed a chronopotentiometry (CP) test in the electrolyte with a three times higher NaCl concentration than seawater, using a 1.0 M KOH + 2.0 M NaCl electrolyte, where the test at 500 mA cm⁻² for 300 h shows no decay.

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer performance in 1.0 M KOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: The AEM electrolyzer needs a cell voltage of only 1.72 V to reach a current density of 1.0 A cm⁻²... the cell efficiency of RuMoNi||RuMoNi... shows a record 77.9% at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² at 1.61 V... it operates at 500 mA cm⁻² for over 240 h.

nodes.description: OER performance comparison in different electrolytes
nodes.source_text: Figure 2b shows that the overpotentials of RuMoNi to achieve 100, 200, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻² only change within 10 mV in the three different electrolytes.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ru, Mo, Ni, O elements present; ex situ Ni 2p indicates surface Ni oxidized from Ni⁰ to Ni²⁺; post-OER Ru 3d peaks at 280.10 eV (Ru⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂) and 284.40 eV (Ru⁴⁺ 3d₃/₂); Mo 3d doublet at 230.4 eV and 233.5 eV (Mo⁶⁺).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicates that the electrocatalyst contains Ru, Mo, Ni, and O (Supplementary Figs. 4–7). Ex situ XPS spectra of Ni 2p show that the Ni atoms on the surface are oxidized from Ni⁰ to Ni²⁺... After the OER process, the XPS spectrum of Ru 3d reveals the valence state of Ru⁴⁺ 3d₅/₂ and Ru⁴⁺ 3d₃/₂ at 280.10 eV and 284.40 eV... In the Mo 3d XPS spectrum (Fig. 4d), a doublet is observed at 230.4 and 233.5 eV (Mo⁶⁺ 3d₅/₂ and Mo⁶⁺ 3d₃/₂).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS reveals uniform distribution of Ni, Ru, and Mo elements over the nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) result reveals the uniform distribution of Ni, Ru, and Mo elements over the nanorods (Fig. 1j).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES indicates Ru content of 0.15 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) results indicate the low content of Ru elements of 0.15 wt%.
The XPS and XRD results show the existence of corrosion-resistant MoO₄²⁻ on the electrode surface... which is consistent with the XRD result of NiMoO₄ (PDF #33-0948) (Fig. 4e).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows NiOOH peaks at 477 cm⁻¹ and 558 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, in situ Raman spectroscopy shows peaks of NiOOH at 477 cm⁻¹ and 558 cm⁻¹ (Supplementary Fig. 10).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES white line shifts to higher energy; FT-EXAFS shows Ni-O at 1.5 Å and Ni-Ni at 2.1 Å, indicating Ni⁰ oxidized to Ni-O coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We use X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) to study Ni valance transformation during the electrochemical oxidation. The white line peak shifts to the higher energy in the Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (Supplementary Fig. 9a).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates used to calculate double layer capacitance Cdl for ECSA determination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double layer capacitance (Cdl) was calculated by CV measurements at scan rates from 10 to 50 mV s⁻¹ in the non-faradaic region.
